title: The Smile of Vessel Farm
premise: Zephyrine Kavanagh, a property surveyor with fifteen years of practiced rationalism, is hired to appraise Vessel Farm — the house her estranged grandmother left her. Every photograph inside now contains an extra chair that wasn't there before, and the house's rooms subtly rearrange to seat an occupant no one will name. As Zephyrine uncovers the founders' unfinished ritual in the well house, she realizes the farm has been auditioning heirs for a century, and the chair is meant for her. To survive, she must complete the ritual before the dry well refills — but finishing it means choosing whether the 'found family' of previous claimants trapped in the walls becomes hers or is finally released. In the end, Zephyrine breaks the cycle by giving the chair away: she names the forgotten founder's daughter as heir, and the house exhales, empty at last.
about_author: I. M. Delacroix is the pen name of a former rural assessor who spent a decade cataloguing properties no one would buy twice. They write horror about houses that keep records.

chapters.title: The Extra Chair
chapters.summary: POV Zephyrine. Arriving to appraise Vessel Farm, she finds every family photograph now includes a plain wooden chair that wasn't there when she was a child. Her rational explanations falter when the chair appears in a photo taken that morning. Emotional beat: dread disguised as professional detachment beginning to crack.

chapters.title: Inventory of Rooms
chapters.summary: POV Zephyrine. She surveys the house room by room; measurements never match twice, and doors she closes are open again. She finds her grandmother's journal, half-burned, warning 'count the seats.' Emotional beat: loneliness meeting the eerie comfort of being expected.

chapters.title: The Founders' Ledger
chapters.summary: POV Zephyrine, with journal excerpts from 1890s founder Abigail Vessel. The ledger lists nine heirs, each 'seated,' each crossed out except one blank line. The well house door, painted shut for decades, stands ajar. Emotional beat: inheritance revealed as obligation, not gift.

chapters.title: Voices in the Walls
chapters.summary: POV Zephyrine. At night she hears the previous claimants whispering through the plaster — not menacing, but pleading, like relatives at a reunion she can't leave. One voice knows her childhood nickname. Emotional beat: terror entangled with longing for belonging.

chapters.title: What the Well Remembers
chapters.summary: POV Zephyrine. She explores the well house and finds it bone-dry but echoing like deep water. Carved rings mark water levels going up, not down. The journal reveals the ritual was interrupted mid-seating. Emotional beat: resolve forming alongside rising panic.

chapters.title: The Surveyor Surveyed
chapters.summary: POV shifting between Zephyrine and the house itself. The rooms begin arranging themselves around her routines; her reflection lags a half-second behind. She understands she is being measured. Emotional beat: loss of control, identity dissolving into property.

chapters.title: Abigail's Daughter
chapters.summary: POV Zephyrine. Through the ledger and a hidden portrait, she learns the ritual's first victim: Abigail's daughter, erased so the house could choose 'worthier' heirs. The whispers sharpen — they want Zephyrine to take the empty seat willingly. Emotional beat: grief for the erased, anger at the design.

chapters.title: Refill
chapters.summary: POV Zephyrine. Rain returns after a drought; the well begins to gurgle and rise. The chair appears physically in the kitchen, facing her place at the table. The claimants' voices turn urgent: finish it tonight or be finished. Emotional beat: deadline pressure, forced commitment.

chapters.title: The Seating
chapters.summary: POV Zephyrine. In the climax, she descends to the well and begins the ritual — but instead of seating herself, she speaks the erased daughter's name into the rings and offers her the heirship. The house convulses; the walls scream; the chair splinters. Emotional beat: defiance as love, sacrifice refused.

chapters.title: Vacancy
chapters.summary: POV Zephyrine, weeks later. The photographs show only people now, no chairs; the whispers are gone, though sometimes she hears a girl laughing in an empty field. She signs the deed over to a land trust and keeps one photo — the daughter, smiling. Emotional beat: bittersweet release, found family honored by letting go.
